answers.answer:
All three SIDs carry the same SCOPe 2.08 lineage: class a (all alpha) > fold a.298 (left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix) > superfamily a.298.1 (TAL effector-like) > family a.298.1.1 (TAL effector). They differ only at the protein level: d2kq5a_ is PthA (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri), d3v6pa_ is dHax3 (Xanthomonas), and d4cj9a_ is BurrH (Burkholderia rhizoxinica). The family placement is therefore a statement about the shared repeat module, not about the full-length proteins.

Why the lengths don't matter: SCOPe classifies one repeat unit per domain, not the whole protein. The d2kq5a_ record is annotated 'single repeat', and the family repeat annotation gives the canonical representative as 4cj9 A:259-292, a 34-residue unit. Natural TAL effectors contain a variable number of these tandem repeats (pretrained knowledge: typically ~1.5 to ~34 per protein), so the full-length length difference reflects repeat count and flanking regions that SCOPe does not count as domains. The 're' inconsistency flag on the family explicitly records that the family-level description applies to all domains even when the common domain is built from a different number of small repeating units. So the same family assignment is compatible with very different whole-protein lengths.

What this supports: the family-level relationship reflects a shared, closely related helix-loop-helix repeat architecture forming a left-handed superhelix. Because SCOPe puts these at family level, the evidence is a close evolutionary relationship among repeat units, and the fold and superfamily labels are consistent with that. It does not show that the three full-length proteins have the same domain count, the same boundaries, or the same DNA-binding specificity; those would need separate evidence (e.g., per-protein sequence or repeat-count analysis). Pretrained knowledge about TAL effector DNA recognition via repeat-variable diresidues at repeat positions 12-13 is not from the SCOPe tools and should not be transferred to these records without that check.

Limits: I did not retrieve full-length protein sequences, so the actual length differences are not measured here. The 4cj9 A:259-292 coordinates are flagged as applying to the canonical representative and not to d2kq5a_ or d3v6pa_ directly, so they must not be copied onto those domains. The SCCS lookup for a.298.1.1 resolved to a species-level node (Burkholderia rhizoxinica, sunid 267706) rather than the family node, so the family conclusion rests on the three domain lineages, not on that node.

answers.answer:
All three SIDs carry the same SCOPe 2.08 lineage: class a (all alpha) > fold a.298 (left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix) > superfamily a.298.1 (TAL effector-like) > family a.298.1.1 (TAL effector). They differ only at the protein level: d2kq5a_ is PthA (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri), d3v6pa_ is dHax3 (Xanthomonas), and d4cj9a_ is BurrH (Burkholderia rhizoxinica). The family placement is therefore a statement about the shared repeat module, not about the full-length proteins.

Why the lengths don't matter: SCOPe classifies one repeat unit per domain, not the whole protein. The d2kq5a_ record is annotated 'single repeat', and the family repeat annotation gives the canonical representative as 4cj9 A:259-292, a 34-residue unit. Natural TAL effectors contain a variable number of these tandem repeats (pretrained knowledge: typically ~1.5 to ~34 per protein), so the full-length length difference reflects repeat count and flanking regions that SCOPe does not count as domains. The 're' inconsistency flag on the family explicitly records that the family-level description applies to all domains even when the common domain is built from a different number of small repeating units. So the same family assignment is compatible with very different whole-protein lengths.

What this supports: the family-level relationship reflects a shared, closely related helix-loop-helix repeat architecture forming a left-handed superhelix. Because SCOPe puts these at family level, the evidence is a close evolutionary relationship among repeat units, and the fold and superfamily labels are consistent with that. It does not show that the three full-length proteins have the same domain count, the same boundaries, or the same DNA-binding specificity; those would need separate evidence (e.g., per-protein sequence or repeat-count analysis). Pretrained knowledge about TAL effector DNA recognition via repeat-variable diresidues at repeat positions 12-13 is not from the SCOPe tools and should not be transferred to these records without that check.

Limits: I did not retrieve full-length protein sequences, so the actual length differences are not measured here. The 4cj9 A:259-292 coordinates are flagged as applying to the canonical representative and not to d2kq5a_ or d3v6pa_ directly, so they must not be copied onto those domains. The SCCS lookup for a.298.1.1 resolved to a species-level node (Burkholderia rhizoxinica, sunid 267706) rather than the family node, so the family conclusion rests on the three domain lineages, not on that node.
